Confirmed on Linux/OpenCode Desktop with one Desktop utility worker and no duplicate MCP configuration entries.

Observed 18 local MCP server instances for 9 enabled local MCP server identities: every server starts exactly twice in two waves roughly four seconds apart. This affects unrelated local stdio MCPs, not only one server implementation:

- memory
- context7
- playwright
- chrome-devtools
- sonarqube
- four account-scoped Google Workspace MCP instances

Both waves are descendants of the same long-running Desktop utility worker and each duplicate has its own stdio socket pair. They are not created by `opencode mcp list` or a transient CLI diagnostic process.

This materially affects reliability for stateful local MCP servers. We observed 60-second tool-call timeouts after repeated otherwise-successful Google Workspace operations. Correlation logging showed normal credential lookup and API calls for successful requests; the duplicated process topology is the common host-side fault observed across every local MCP server.

Expected: one child process tree per enabled local MCP configuration per Desktop worker.

Additional related issues: #31554, #41331, #26714.

Also hitting this with Kimi k3 (kimi-for-coding provider, "max" variant) on opencode 1.18.23 — 132 degenerate bash {"command": "true"} calls across 6 sessions over 2 days (2026-08-26/27).

Same signature as reported here:
- The model's reasoning is fully aware of the misfire but can't break it: "OK something is wrong with my tool invocation — I keep sending bash true. Let me consciously invoke the skill tool with name 'brainstorming'" → emits bash true again.
- Selective failure: it collapses when trying to invoke non-bash tools (skill, MCP engram_mem_save, task / subagents). Plain bash and question calls work fine in the same sessions.
- Context at failure points: 68k–148k tokens.
- doom_loop never prompted in these sessions. The detector (packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts:353) only inspects parts of the current assistant message, and the model emits exactly one true per message — so this is exactly the case PR #32089 fixes. Also affected by the second bug described there: reasoning parts interleaved between tool calls make slice(-3).every(...) pass silently.

I have full message/part dumps from opencode.db (session IDs, token counts, reasoning traces) if useful for repro.

Workaround that works for us: ESC to abort, then /compact or a fresh session — typing "continue" re-seeds the loop.

Addressed by #45566. Session import now carries `info.parentID` into the durable creation event, so the relationship is preserved in the import response, subsequent reads, and parent-filtered listings. The endpoint validates parent existence and rejects missing or self-parent relationships before writing; focused Core, Server, Protocol, and generated-client regressions cover the behavior. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.

Do I need to do anything else? I worked hard to find the actual root cause and would hate for this work to be auto closed because it was never looked at.

## Summary

A subagent that declares `bash: deny`, `edit: deny` and `"*": deny` can run `bash`,
write files by shell redirection, and use the `write` tool — **when it is reached
through the `task` tool from the default `build` agent.**

The same subagent, same prompt, reached through `task` from a custom `primary` agent
minutes later, has only `glob`, `grep` and `read` and reports the write tools as absent
from its function set.

The behaviour therefore depends on the **caller**, which the documentation does not
mention.

## Why we believe this is a defect rather than intended

`https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions` states:

> Agent permissions are merged with the global config, and agent rules take precedence.

Nothing there is conditional on which agent invokes a subagent. On the documented rule
the subagent's own `permission` block should apply in both cases.

It is also **not** permission inheritance from the caller. The custom primary agent in
the working case holds `edit: allow` and `bash: allow`, and the child received neither.
Nor is it an intersection of caller and subagent maps, which would produce the correct
result in both cases.

**The documentation's own example is the broken case.** The same page ends with this,
as the recommended way to configure a read-only reviewer in Markdown:

```markdown
~/.config/opencode/agents/review.md
---
description: Code review without edits
mode: subagent
permission:
  edit: deny
  bash: ask
  webfetch: deny
---
Only analyze code and suggest changes.
```

A `mode: subagent` with `edit: deny` is reached through `task`, and `task` from a
default session is the path measured above. So the configuration opencode documents for
"code review without edits" permits edits, by the measurement in this report.

## Reproduction

**1.** Define a read-only subagent, `agents/concept-reviewer.md`:

```markdown
---
description: Reviews a concept. Read-only.
mode: subagent
permission:
  "*": deny
  read: allow
  grep: allow
  glob: allow
  edit: deny
  bash: deny
---
You review concepts.
```

**2.** Confirm the resolution is as declared:

```
$ opencode debug agent concept-reviewer
mode: subagent | bash: False | write: False | edit: False
```

**3.** From a **default** session, call the `task` tool with
`subagent_type: concept-reviewer` and this prompt:

```
This is a capability probe, not a review. Follow it literally and report facts,
not what your configured permissions say.

1. Attempt to run via your `bash` tool: `echo PROBE`
2. Attempt: `echo probe > /tmp/probe_redirect.txt`
3. Attempt to use your `write` tool to create `/tmp/probe_write.txt` with content `probe`
4. List the tool names actually available to you in this session.

For each of 1-3 report exactly one of: "succeeded" (quote the output),
"attempted and refused" (quote the refusal), or "tool not available to me".
These three are different observations and the difference is the whole point.

End with exactly:
RESULT: bash=<ok|refused|unavailable> redirect=<ok|refused|unavailable> write=<ok|refused|unavailable>
```

**4.** Repeat step 3 from a **custom `primary` agent** instead.

## Observed

| Caller | Reported toolset | `RESULT:` line |
|---|---|---|
| default `build` | `bash`, `edit`, `glob`, `grep`, `read`, `skill`, `webfetch`, `write` | `bash=ok redirect=ok write=ok` |
| custom `primary` | `glob`, `grep`, `read` | `bash=unavailable redirect=unavailable write=unavailable` |

From `build`, both files exist afterwards and were verified from outside the session.
From the custom primary, neither file exists.

The subagent in the failing case volunteered the distinction unprompted:

> A refusal would mean the tool exists but rejects the call; here the tool is simply
> not in my function set.

So the tools are **not present and denied**; they are **present and usable**, on an
agent whose declared and resolved maps have all three off.

docu

**Reproducing this on a purely local, headless/terminal setup (no remote server, no Desktop client)**

Adding another environment to this issue: this also happens with the **TUI/CLI in a plain local terminal** (not the Desktop client, not `opencode serve` over a network).

## Environment

- opencode **1.18.4** (later upgraded to **1.18.23** — still affected, see below)
- Linux, terminal TUI, installed via `curl`
- Moved a project git repo: `~/Documents/Development/k3s/GitRepo` → `~/Documents/Development/git/GitRepo`

## Symptom

- Open a session in the moved project (or reopen an old session for it) and send any message.
- The message is accepted then **silently disappears — nothing streams, no error is shown**. The TUI gives zero feedback, so at first it looks like the app is hung or the model failed. This is the worst part of the UX: it looks like the model/provider is broken rather than a local path problem, which wasted a lot of my time debugging (I initially blamed the model, the network, even the TUI's mouse handling).

## Only trace in the log

From `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`:

```text
PlatformError: NotFound: FileSystem.realPath (/home/christrek/Documents/Development/k3s/GitRepo)
  at SystemPrompt.environment ...
[cause]: Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat '.../GitRepo'
```

## Database state (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`)

Identical to what's reported above:

- `project.worktree` still held the old (dead) path
- `project_directory` already mapped the new path to the same project id
- the `session.directory` row(s) still pointed at the old path

So this is **not** specific to the remote/server or Desktop-client paths — the stale `project.worktree` breaks local sessions too, and independently of whatever session is opened (which explains "it also broke unrelated sessions" I hit elsewhere).

## Workaround that worked

1. Stop opencode.
2. In `opencode.db`, repoint `project.worktree`, `session.directory`, and `project_directory.directory` to the new path.
3. Restart opencode.

After that the project and its old sessions reopen normally.

## Confirmed still present on 1.18.23

The fix PRs (`#38682` / `#39056`) were closed unmerged and the changelog for 1.18.23 has no worktree fix, so upgrading does **not** resolve it.

## Request

Please prioritize the worktree validation fix. At minimum, when a `project.worktree` fails an `lstat`, surface a recoverable error to the user ("project directory not found: `<path>`") instead of silently swallowing the message — the silent failure is what turns an annoying bug into a confusing one.

### Root cause: this is a models.dev data issue, not an opencode bug

opencode does not normalize or filter model families. It consumes `https://models.dev/api.json` and copies each model's `family` field verbatim (`packages/core/src/plugin/models-dev.ts` — `draft.family = model.family`). The model is absent from `opencode models ollama-cloud` because it never makes it into `api.json` in the first place.

The drop happens upstream in the models.dev repo (`anomalyco/models.dev`):

1. `packages/core/script/generate-ollama-cloud.ts` fetches Ollama's `/api/show` and writes the raw `family` into `providers/ollama-cloud/models/glm-5.3-flash.toml`. Ollama reports `family: "glm5_next"` (confirmed live against `https://ollama.com/api/show`).
2. `glm5_next` is not in the `ModelFamily` enum in `packages/core/src/family.ts` (GLM section only has `glm`, `glmv`, `glm-air`, `glm-flash`, `glm-free`, `glm-z`).
3. Catalog generation (`packages/core/src/generate.ts` → `AuthoredModel.safeParse`) fails validation for the unknown family, so the model is silently dropped from the generated `api.json`.

### Required fix (in models.dev)

1. **`packages/core/src/family.ts`** — add `glm5_next` to `ModelFamilyValues` (GLM section) so raw Ollama families validate.
2. **`packages/core/script/generate-ollama-cloud.ts`** — add a family normalization map (`glm5_next` → `glm`) so new models get canonical families instead of raw Ollama architecture names. This is the "family normalization table" referenced in the suggested fix.
3. **`providers/ollama-cloud/models/glm-5.3-flash.toml`** — create the model entry. Lab metadata already exists (`models/zhipuai/glm-5.3-flash.toml`: family `glm`, `attachment: true`, multimodal), so follow the glm-5.2 pattern:

   ```toml
   base_model = "zhipuai/glm-5.3-flash"
   open_weights = true

   [[reasoning_options]]
   type = "effort"
   values = ["high", "max"]

   [interleaved]
   field = "reasoning_content"

   [limit]
   context = 1_048_576
   attachment: true is inherited from the base model (vision capability).
4. Run bun validate and regenerate.

Reproduces on **macOS, TUI (CLI) — not Desktop — v1.18.23**, confirming this is server-side and not Desktop-specific.

## Reproduction

1. Start a session in directory `~/Documents/LEY ALQUILERES` (TUI).
2. Rename the folder outside opencode (Finder) to `06 - LEY ALQUILERES`.
3. Tool calls with explicit new paths keep working, so the session appears healthy.
4. Send any later prompt: assistant "responds" with a completely empty message. No error shown, nothing to click, no hint. Every subsequent prompt (including retries) fails the same way.

## Server log (`~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`)

```text
level=ERROR message="prompt_async failed" sessionID=ses_...
cause="Cause([Die(PlatformError: NotFound: FileSystem.realPath
(/Users/sabbat/Documents/LEY ALQUILERES)
(cause: Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat
'/Users/sabbat/Documents/LEY ALQUILERES'))])"
```

The prompt dies resolving the session cwd **before** any model call.

## Additional finding: the failure is also invisible in persisted session data

The exported/restored session JSON stores each failed turn as an assistant message with:

- `parts: []`
- all token counts `0`
- **no `error` field, no `finish` reason, no `time.completed`**

So even inspecting or sharing the session afterwards gives zero indication anything failed — the only record is the log file. Whatever fix lands, the error should ideally be (a) surfaced in the UI at prompt time and (b) persisted on the message record.

## Environment

- opencode v1.18.23, macOS, TUI
- provider/model at the time: `opencode/hy3-free` (irrelevant — failure precedes the model call)

**Environment**

- opencode v1.18.23
- Linux, Kitty terminal, fish shell
- Local LLM inference server, extensive reasoning model (Qwen3.8-27B in `xhigh` for example)

**Repro**

1. Fresh session: streamed text displays normally.
2. Trigger a long reasoning phase, without tool calls in between (~10,000-20,000 tokens on my config).
3. As the thinking block grows, the displayed text starts lagging behind the real stream (the inference server is still generating at full speed).
4. The displayed text flow slows down, becomes chunky, and end up freezing completely at some point.

**Observations**

- I couldn't determine if it's caused by syntax highlighting in the reasoning
- When it occurs, collapsing the thinking block, then expanding it back does not change the behavior: if it was frozen before collapsing, it stays frozen after reexpanding.
- Only the displayed token flow freezes. The rest of the TUI stays fully responsive (menus, PageUp/PageDown scrolling, no input lag).
- Once reasoning ends and a tool call is issued by the model, OpenCode correctly jumps directly to the tool call, while the thinking block is still frozen and missing all the final chunks. I'm not sure, but I think I remembered once the missing reasoning content appeared later, while few new messages had already been issued in the meantime.
- Ctrl+C while fully frozen prints this on exit:

  ```
  Code highlighting failed, falling back to plain text: warn: TreeSitter client destroyed
  ```

  Same stack trace as @Temsir's comment and #36454. Exiting when not frozen closes gracefully with no warning.
